summary: Root cause: system-auditor's notebook cycle-log compose step (main.md Step 1a-h / notebook-write SKILL.md AC-3) is 100% LLM-narrated prose requiring byte-for-byte reproduction of the entire existing file in one tool call, with no deterministic actuator (unlike the commit step, already hardened into scripts/auditor-notebook-commit.sh for the identical class of defect). The AC-2a immutability pre-commit gate that exists specifically to catch retained-section mutation is warn-by-default (never blocks) and has fired >=6 unactioned times on this exact file since 2026-07-30; worse, its detection algorithm treats a heading that disappears from staged content as an authorized 'whole section drop' with no corroborating file-size-shrinkage check, so this incident's exact shape (heading blanked, body orphaned, file did NOT shrink) would sail through undetected even in reject mode. A corroborating, independent process-integrity finding: the commit step itself bypassed the mandated auditor-notebook-commit.sh script this cycle (a bare git commit tripped the repo's sweep-guard hook and was escalated-rejected 3 seconds before the corrupted content landed via a retried pathspec-scoped commit) -- prior_warns=7 already in-session, its own recurring-bug candidate. User-flagged hypothesis (shared root cause with notebook-auto-prune.sh's pm.md-class newest-first/oldest-first ordering bug) was mechanically RULED OUT: the file was 80/81 lines and 6017/~6020 bytes, both far under the governed 200L/12000B caps, so that hook's drop-oldest logic never even entered its section-parsing code path for this write -- and that ordering bug is independently confirmed already-generically-fixed in the live script (self-deriving direction per file with tie-break voting, not a hardcoded assumption).
